newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil gold rights sale attracts foreign interest.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gold rights sale attracts foreign interest.

text.p: Three major international firms have already shown interest in the exploration rights of a possible gold reserve in Brazil's northern Rondonia state, said a spokesman at the Mineral Resources Survey Company (CPRM).
The rights to the Rio Jaru region are the first to be put up for sale within the National Gold Prospecting Program by the CPRM, which is part of the country's Mines and Energy Ministry.
Initial surveys show the area could contain between 15 and 30 tonnes of gold.
Companies which have already expressed interest in the site include Canada's Barrick Gold, Anglo-Australian RTZ-CRA and South Africa's Gencor, said Victor Hugo, the CPRM's press officer.
Those firms interested in winning the exploration rights have until February 3 to submit a proposal to the CPRM. Nine companies have so far bought the necessary documents, Hugo said.

Interested parties have to be prepared to pay a tax of 100,000 reais ($96,000), invest a minimum of two million reais ($1.92 million) over two years in surveys and pay at least two percent a year in royalties.
The winner is likely to be announced in March, Hugo said.
The next area to be considered will be in Eldorado, in the Vale do Ribeira area of Sao Paulo state, Hugo said.
No date has yet been fixed for the submission of proposals but it is likely to be only after the Rio Jaru rights have been awarded, he added.
